g3ela-26-1-teach-morph: [curious] Some word parts tell you about shape. Form means shape. Here's a word that's not on your list. Platform. Plat means flat. So a platform is a flat shape you stand on, like at a train station. Flat shape: platform! Read the four words and their parts. Then tap See what was hiding, and type the missing parts.
g3ela-26-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Superior. Here's the sentence. Edmund gave a very superior look, as if he were far older than Lucy. One, read the sentence: he's acting older and better. Two, look for word parts: super means above. Three, check it. Superior means acting as if you're above someone. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.
g3ela-26-1-teach-gram: [warmly] A story can happen in the past, or right now. Once you pick a time, the verbs stay there. Listen. Edmund climbed onto the sledge and sits down. Climbed is past. Sits is now! It slipped. It should be sat. Read The Rule box, and tap Now check your thinking. Then find every verb that slipped.
g3ela-26-1-teach-spell: Clap with me. Dan, ger, ous. Dangerous. Three claps! Each beat has one vowel sound. Now try beautiful. Beau, ti, ful. Beau has two vowel letters, but only one sound, so it's one beat. Count the sounds, not the letters. Clap the words in Group A and Group B, and tap See the Rule. Then sort the words.
g3ela-26-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Find form, and remember: it means shape. Formless. Form, plus less, without. Formless means without a shape, like a cloud of fog. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-26-2-teach-vocab: Here's a strong word from Chapter 5. Beastly. Peter says Edmund has been perfectly beastly to Lu. Acting like a beast? Very mean! Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.
g3ela-26-2-teach-gram: Which verb slipped? Susan looked inside and sees only coats. Looked is past. Sees is now. Sees slipped! It should be saw. Find the slipped verb in each sentence, and tap Now check your thinking. Then fix the paragraph.
g3ela-26-2-teach-spell: Beat detective time! Which word has two beats? Wardrobe. Lamp. Enchanted. Clap them. Ward, robe: two! Lamp: one. En, chant, ed: three. Wardrobe it is. Read the rule. Then in each row, tap the one word that matches.
g3ela-26-2-teach-rwm: [warmly] Let's try all three parts with a different sentence from Chapter 5. Edmund, who was becoming a nastier person every minute, thought that he had scored a great success. Part one, read like a reader. Edmund thinks he won, but he hurt Lucy. Part two, read like a writer. Lewis tucks a fact about Edmund into the middle, with who. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: Opti, who was getting sleepier every minute, thought that one more chapter would do. Now it's your turn with the sentence about Edmund being tired. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-26-3-teach-morph: Snap the parts together. Form. At. Format! The format of a page is its shape: where the title goes, and where the words go. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-26-3-teach-vocab: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. Edmund gave Lucy a blank look, as if he were much older. Beastly? Hmm, no. Superior? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.
g3ela-26-3-teach-gram: Let's move a sentence into the past. The children run upstairs and hide in the wardrobe. Run becomes ran. Hide becomes hid. The children ran upstairs and hid in the wardrobe. Read the before and after. Then rewrite the two sentences so every verb is in the past.
g3ela-26-3-teach-spell: Let's split a long word into chunks. Professor. Pro, fes, sor. Three chunks! Say each chunk, then push them back together: Professor. Read the rule. Then say each word in chunks, and tap the card to check.
g3ela-26-4-teach-morph: Quick! What does form mean? Shape! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Landform. A landform is a shape of the land, like a hill or a valley. Now tap Roll the Dice. Say what each word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six.
g3ela-26-4-teach-vocab: Here's how I'd use a word about the story. Superior. Edmund gave Lucy a superior look when he said they were only pretending. One word, one moment. Now choose one of your words and write your own sentence about Chapters 4 to 6.
g3ela-26-4-teach-gram: Three passes, like an editor. Lucy said the queen was terrible and edmund feels sick. Pass one, capitals: Queen and Edmund. Pass two, verbs: feels slipped, so it becomes felt. Pass three, a comma before and. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.
g3ela-26-4-teach-spell: Here's my roll. Inquisitive. In, quis, i, tive. Four beats! How did I know? Four vowel sounds. Tap Roll the dice, split the word out loud, and say how you knew. Then tap Check my answer.
